criteria.criterion: A test on the cutover fixture lands a new job branch (intervention commit, records-only commit, job landing) through land_pr with a squash merge. The squash commit on main and the three pull-request commits reached from the records branch have no Athena- lines. The landing record classifies them. check --history and check --attribution report no violations. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: post_c0_landing_through_land_pr passed when I ran it. Steps: intervene --with-staged, then ask/go, then land_through_pr (land_pr with the FakeHost squash). It asserts that the squash commit is the remote main, that the landing-record kinds are DeclaredIntervention, then RecordsOnly…, then JobLanding, and that none of those commits, the landed commit or the squash has an Athena- line. The landed commit must be reachable from the records tip. The real `athena check --history` must report 0 violation(s) and `--attribution` 0 finding(s). The test allows len >= 3 because go adds extra records-only commits. The test is in athena-cli, not athena-core (see findings), and it is included in the recorded full suite, which passed.

criteria.criterion: A test covers retry_landing for a blocked job after C0: no trailer search, no 'closing commit not found' bail, and no Athena-Verified-Content written. Run: cargo test -p athena-core retry_landing.
criteria.evidence: retry_landing_after_c0_searches_no_trailer_and_writes_none passed when I ran it. It blocks a post-C0 job with a local edit, restores the file, and calls go again, which runs retry_landing. The result is Landed, the commit message has no 'Athena-' text and the commit holds outcome-landed.json. landed_commit_for finds that commit, and it then lands through land_pr. In run.rs the trailer search, the bail and the Athena-Verified-Content push all sit in the `!stopped` branch. The paired test retry_landing_without_a_cutover_job_still_writes_trailers also passed. The criterion's literal command `-p athena-core retry_landing` ran 0 tests, because the tests are in athena-cli.

criteria.criterion: Tests call athena status's trace and the auditor through their real entry points on a post-C0 job and get correct results. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: post_c0_job_is_read_by_the_trace_and_the_auditor passed. Athena::trace returns state 'landed' with an outcome, and its commits include the squash commit. In a fresh clone with athena/records fetched, the old trailer-only lookup fails with 'none could be read', while Athena::audit succeeds and returns an audit whose target is the job.

criteria.criterion: With no cutover_job configured, trailers are written as before. All existing tests pass, cargo clippy is clean and cargo fmt --check passes. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks passed: tests (1335), clippy and fmt. message_for_parent leaves the message unchanged when no cutover_job is set, and the gate's new rules only apply when trailers_stopped is true. The gate test covers both settings and passed when I ran it. retry_landing_without_a_cutover_job_still_writes_trailers also passed.

findings.evidence: The planned demonstrations included invariant.rs. The others are the staged-intervention writer and test files. Each is needed to strip the trailers at every writer, or to keep the pre-C0 tests on trailers, and D133 explains them.

findings.summary: After C0 the gate accepts a records-only commit by its content alone, so a records commit is no longer tied to a named job.
findings.evidence: `if trailers_stopped(git, change) && touches_records(judged) { return Ok(Vec::new()); }` replaces names_existing_work for post-C0 commits. D133 records this as a known tradeoff. It also notes that code_health.rs still counts landings by trailer and needs its own follow-up change.

summary: The change does what was asked. Once athena.toml at a commit's parent names [history] cutover_job, the commit writers (Committer::build_commit_in through message_for_parent, plus the staged-intervention commit in manage.rs) strip Athena- trailers. To match, the gate, the landed-commit lookup, the squash text, retry_landing, the status trace and the auditor were changed to work without trailers. I ran the new tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/trailer_stop.rs and all 4 passed. They use the existing k0tt cutover fixture and only real entry points: intervene, ask/go, land_pr through land_through_pr, retry_landing through go, Athena::trace, Athena::audit, and the real `athena check --history` and `--attribution` binaries. The paired test with no cutover_job shows trailers are still written. The new gate unit test passed too. Athena's recorded runs of fmt, clippy and the full test suite (1335 tests) all passed. The docs record the design, the rejected alternatives and how retry_landing behaves after C0. They also say why nothing was removed: the stale "retry_landing has no test" text does not exist, which my own search confirmed. There are two minor findings. First, the new tests live in athena-cli, so the commands named in criteria 1 and 2 (`cargo test -p athena-core ...`) run none of them; the full suite does. Second, several changed files are not on the expected-deliverables list, though each is needed and explained.
